prompt:
Below is an excerpt from a company annual report.

The graph assumes $100 was invested on 12/31/2013 in Cedar Systems Inc. common stock and in each index, with dividends reinvested. The table shows the value of each investment at each date.

|  | 12/31/2013 | 12/31/2014 | 12/31/2015 | 12/31/2016 | 12/31/2017 | 12/31/2018 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cedar Systems Inc. | $ 100.00 | $ 107.00 | $ 119.32 | $ 151.32 | $ 162.76 | $ 177.94 |
| Nasdaq composite | $ 100.00 | $ 112.67 | $ 107.89 | $ 118.14 | $ 135.22 | $ 164.03 |
| S&P 400 information technology | $ 100.00 | $ 91.95 | $ 92.63 | $ 85.04 | $ 103.75 | $ 121.52 |

Question: Over the three years from 12/31/2015 to 12/31/2018, what was the difference, in percentage points, between the total return of Cedar Systems Inc. and the total return of the Nasdaq composite?

Work through the calculation, then end your reply with one final line in exactly this form:
ANSWER: <number>
Give the number only, without a % sign, rounded to 2 decimals. Use a negative number if Cedar Systems Inc. is lower.

metadata.source: synthetic numbers; table shape adapted from FinQA record CDNS/2015/page_30.pdf-3 (MIT, Chen et al. 2021)
metadata.why_hard: The window starts mid-table, so 'value - 100' (the shortcut that works from the $100 base) is wrong; each return must be end/start - 1.
